canal_p10_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_001.text: The twenty-first morning was quiet enough that Yue could hear a dropped measuring peg bounce twice on the dry paving. Bao marked the upper pocket's present test depth on the side ruler: twenty centimetres, holding twenty-four of the canal's checked ten-litre jar equivalents. That was an ordinary measurement unit, not drinking water promised to anyone. The feeder would fill only this prepared pocket. The lower stop kept its current closure above the gardens, and the trial outlet led into its checked nearby catch channel.

canal_p10_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_002.text: Luo walked the catch channel before accepting it for tomorrow's bounded discharge. The small fitted side-release would empty the pocket there while the lower stop stayed closed above the gardens. The catch returned to the canal above the downstream spur, with its accessible grate cleared and footing fenced. The old whole-diversion map led elsewhere. Today's catch was checked for this small trial volume and flow. Yue drew the routes separately because their lines approached one another on the page. Two nearby blue strokes could make very different promises.

canal_p10_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_003.text: Bao checked the stop's fixed witness marks after its first small bucket wetting. The brace stayed seated, and the replaced sealing run showed no new twist. He retained the temporary working limit rather than calling the repeated dry check a stronger rating. Jiang's mechanical inspection accepted the control path, but the live trial still required the feeder head checked at the moment of opening. Yue copied the side-ruler mark and independent fixed masonry reference and cleaned the gauge face with the cloth Tian had given her. Its ordinary visibility would matter more than its polish.

canal_p10_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_004.text: The live trial had a short booked cargo hold, which the landing receivers confirmed that morning. Two boats chose earlier departures; one chose the upstream transfer rather than wait. Their choices stayed outside the trial account. Han's useful private-gear service observations continued around the hold, and his clerk counted actual work rather than estimating customers who might have arrived. Yue watched an empty boat slip past the new gate and felt the bank's normal life continue around a small space reserved for asking a careful question.

canal_p10_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_005.text: Luo called the observers to the upper apron for the final ground walk. The inner paving stayed sound under ordinary viewing, while the outer hollow remained fenced. The porter rest marker was clear of their positions. Nobody would step into the test pocket to improve a reading after water entered. The moving stop board had its own guarded line. Yue knew the plan now and wanted to run through it quickly. Luo made her walk the actual retreat anyway. Knowledge in a room did not show whether yesterday's basket had been left in the path.

canal_p10_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_006.text: A basket had been left beside the inner corner, full of the keeper's clean cloths. Luo moved it herself and apologized to the porter receiver rather than treating her own household thing as somehow exempt from the work line. Yue helped carry it to the shed after its contents were tied. The final walk gained a concrete reason for repetition. Tian came out with the seedling still on her window ledge and said she hoped it would not be blamed next. Luo told her the plant could keep its innocent height.

canal_p10_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_007.text: The morning-only observer asked whether tomorrow's live interval would truly end before his booked boat. Jiang's remaining paid trial hours allowed a short inspection and controlled sequence, with any further work scheduled rather than borrowed from his departure. Luo confirmed that his observation appointment ended at its stated time even if the test stopped early. He would still receive payment for accepted work. The sentence steadied him more than a speech about common effort. Yue wondered how many old work calls had relied on a person being too embarrassed to ask it aloud.

canal_p10_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_008.text: At the store, Jiang gave Yue the unpowered selector comparison tile and asked her to trace the intended command path. The route remained the small earned arm path used for the gate, within the quarter-unit command and half-unit delivery allowance. Yue would make one prepared selection at the live stop test if actual conditions permitted. The powered actuator would move the side-release from its own supply. Jiang kept the selector and ordinary geared manual release ready beside it. The test could finish without making Yue's success the only way everyone could go home.

canal_p10_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_009.text: Yue asked whether doing the same small command again counted as progress. Jiang said she could compare its actual stability after recovery, but a new reliable performance did not open a third pair. The body had its own work ahead. Yue wanted both reliability and the next threshold, and hearing them separated still disappointed her. Jiang handed the cold tile back and said disappointment could be present without running the test. Yue put it down before practicing again merely to improve her mood.

canal_p10_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_010.text: The current supply record held two hundred sixteen units in the six original purchased stones. Jiang gave the live response a conservative eighteen-unit maximum across its checked sequence and any accepted short follow-up. An early stop might use less. The actual gauge would determine the count written afterward. No one would spend the whole allowance because a plan had made it available. Yue recorded the maximum and the clear rule that an interrupted task could leave charge unspent. The lower bound after this trial would be one hundred ninety-eight.

canal_p10_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_011.text: The feeder's hand control had a stiff turn at its first opening. Luo inspected it with the flow isolated and found ordinary grit at the accessible pin. She cleaned and lubricated the working face, then repeated its full closed-to-limited movement. The small feed could be controlled at its intended notch. Yue wanted to ask whether Jiang's relay should open it instead. The keeper said the ordinary hand mechanism did its job after cleaning. A powered solution would add a path they did not need to solve a handful of grit.

canal_p10_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_012.text: Tian took the cargo-hold notice to the sail owner she had worked for. He asked whether she approved of every stop now that the public hearing gave her hours back. She said this one had an actual limit and ordinary alternatives. He said she sounded like the bank's apprentice. She said she was still the seamstress he owed nothing further because the finished order was paid. Yue laughed when Tian reported it later. The response had allowed both a good argument and the more useful fact that her own transaction was complete.

canal_p10_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_013.text: At noon, the down-fork garden correspondent sent another map with the accepted twenty-fourth-day visit confirmed. A recent private drainage cut appeared on it, crossing near the old spill route. The gardeners wanted it observed before any lower water release. Bao marked it as offered current information, not an engineering acceptance. The first upper trial stayed above their closure. The map made the larger repair feel less straightforward, which was useful now rather than a catastrophe discovered after the bank sent water toward somebody else's planted rows.

canal_p10_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_014.text: Han brought the current private-gear observations to Luo: useful actual loading intervals, one canceled request and a maintenance check done on his own stock. The later lease was still proposed. He also asked whether the trial could lend him its viewing crowd for a notice about the surplus hoist sale. Tian said people could read it at his store without standing in a guarded work line. Han agreed and moved the notice there. Yue liked that the bank's regained freedom sometimes appeared as nothing more grand than a poster being put in a different place.

canal_p10_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_015.text: Before evening, Bao fitted the ordinary splash screen beside the catch channel. It protected viewers from the bounded outlet without hiding the side ruler or obstructing the working retreat. The screen used purchased material already assigned to that part of the trial, and its ordinary tie stayed clear of the selector guard. Yue checked the sight line from the observer's actual height. Her first drawing placed the screen too high, as if everyone on the bank shared her eyes. She lowered it to the planned opening and saw the marked waterline clearly.

canal_p10_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_016.text: The observers rehearsed the stop call once more with the screen in place. The morning-only worker could see the gauge, but the nearer relay speaker could not see his face from her current position. Luo moved that position within the checked apron rather than asking him to lean around the screen. Their spoken calls came clearly after the adjustment. Tian said the arrangement looked less tidy than the first chalk dots. Bao said the chalk could move more easily than a person trying not to fall. Yue changed the drawing.

canal_p10_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_017.text: That night, Yue wrote the orchard appointment request's actual message receipt beside her personal fare notes. The letter had been dispatched, but the matron had not answered. The third morning after canal closure remained a proposed date. Any personal visit owed under her retained earlier arrangement stayed unfulfilled. The difference weighed on her more after arranging so many other people's ending times. She wanted the next promise to survive its contact with the calendar, and that would require an answer from someone whose day was not hers to assign.

canal_p10_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_018.text: On the twenty-second morning, Luo checked the feeder's current head before anyone opened the case. It stayed within the trial limit. The lower stop and catch channel were clear, the ground route remained fenced and the booked cargo hold began at its actual time. Jiang inspected the supply isolation and guard, then confirmed the accepted dry work remained unchanged. Bao read the witness marks. Yue stood in her prepared place with her route recovered, hearing the morning-only observer give his own ready call instead of being counted by somebody else's glance.

canal_p10_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_019.text: The first feed entered the pocket at the keeper's limited hand-control notch. Dry clay darkened slowly, following the old small-bucket wetting before spreading wider. The observer read the side ruler while another watched the stop's fixed mark. Yue wanted the water to arrive in a smooth bright sheet like the training drawings. It moved in irregular little tongues around ordinary surface hollows. Jiang had not asked it to be beautiful. She asked for actual readings, and Yue wrote the times in a hand that shook slightly from wanting them right.

canal_p10_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_020.text: At the first low mark, the pocket's water soaked into a dry edge more quickly than its center. Luo held the feed at the planned notch rather than increasing it to defeat the soil. Bao watched the lower stop for unintended passing water. None appeared at its accepted closure. The catch channel remained dry before the planned response test. A child at the public viewing place asked if they were pouring away a drink. Tian explained that this was ordinary canal water measured for a mechanism test, with household drinking supply elsewhere.

canal_p10_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_021.text: The water reached the intermediate mark without shifting the brace. Jiang asked Yue for her sensation check before the prepared command. Her opened arm routes matched the recovered baseline; she could perform the small sequence once. The actual command would select the side-release response after the pocket reached its checked maximum, and Jiang could use the manual fallback if needed. Yue said she was ready, then heard the observer give an unexpected stop word. His voice was clear enough that no one could pretend the call belonged to a passing boat.

canal_p10_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_022.text: He had seen the water climb a dark line below the side ruler faster than its marked rise suggested. Luo closed the feeder immediately while the pocket remained below its maximum. Jiang kept the actuator isolated from a live command. Bao watched the ordinary stop and called its current brace still seated. The observer apologized while continuing to stand at his assigned mark. Yue wanted to tell him it was only wet clay. Instead she asked him to show the line from his safe position, because the stopping procedure had brought them to this exact question.

canal_p10_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_023.text: The line lay near a narrow crack at the pocket's edge, where water could wick above its visible surface. Bao would compare it only after the current water was safely held or drained through the checked catch. The observer had not claimed a broken stop; he had called an unexplained reading under the agreed rule. The trial clock continued toward his ending time. Yue could feel her hoped-for perfect sequence shrinking while the bank discovered something its drawings did not know. That discovery was part of the trial, however inconvenient its hour.

canal_p10_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_024.text: Jiang said the prepared live command remained unspent. The actual apparatus draw so far was zero; ordinary hand feed and fitted wood had held the pocket's initial water. The crew could choose a checked stop response, end the live interval and return after ordinary examination, or keep the feed closed while comparing the accessible ruler from stable paving. Each permitted option kept the lower closure and clear ground route. Nobody would step into the water to settle an argument faster. Yue was asked for her observation, not authority to overrule a stopping voice.

canal_p10_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_025.text: Tian stood near the public viewing place with the current stopping rule on its board. One impatient spectator called the observer timid. Tian told him the trial required the call when a reading left its explanation; if he wanted a show without interruption, this was the wrong place to wait. The observer heard her and straightened. Yue envied how quickly Tian could choose a firm sentence now that her own work hours were no longer offered for sale. Then she remembered the corrected accusation Tian had struggled to remove before the hearing.

canal_p10_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_026.text: Bao checked the pocket's actual held water against the side ruler without approaching its wet edge. The measured surface stayed below the maximum. The dark line could be wicking, a misleading gauge face or flow into a shallow side hollow. Each explanation would lead to a different ordinary correction. Jiang kept the supply off while they considered the permitted next step. The question would not be answered by feeding harder or widening Yue's command. It would be answered by choosing what to examine while the current controlled state still made examination possible.

canal_p10_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_027.text: The morning-only observer reminded Luo that his boat would leave after the accepted interval. She confirmed his ending time and asked the nearer relay speaker to preserve his offered account for the follow-up. Nobody would hold him in place until the water made his first call look wise or foolish. Yue saw how tempting that would be: keep the person beside the anomaly until a neat result cleared everyone's feeling. The bank could finish the test later. He had another ordinary route to take today.

canal_p10_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_028.text: Jiang offered the three checked paths again, speaking slowly enough for every current worker to hear. They could perform the prepared stop and drain response, leave the pocket safely held for ordinary ruler comparison, or end the live interval and conduct the examination before an accepted later follow-up. The maximum eighteen-unit supply budget and actual hired hours remained limits. Yue chose how to contribute her small command and observation. The initial stop had already been honored. Now the next choice would determine what kind of evidence followed it.

canal_p10_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_029.text: The feed remained closed, and the pocket's actual surface stayed below its marked maximum. Yue could join the prepared drain response, compare the gauge while the wood held its current small head or end today's live work for a dry examination and scheduled return. The observer's stopping call would remain in the record whichever path she took. Success would mean discovering the pocket's real behavior inside the limits they had made, rather than punishing someone for interrupting the result Yue had wanted before the first water entered.

choices.text: Perform the prepared side-drain response, then rebook the test.
Hold the feed closed and compare the gauge from stable ground.
End live work today and examine the emptied pocket.

canal_p10_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_030.text: Jiang accepted the prepared drain response while Luo kept the feeder closed. Bao confirmed the side-release's catch clear and the lower stop above the gardens still seated. Yue checked her route once, then formed the quarter-unit command within its half-unit delivery allowance. The side actuator opened into the checked catch, using eight counted supply units. Water left the pocket in an uneven bright stream. The morning-only observer watched from his assigned mark, seeing his stopping call become an actual controlled end rather than a rebuke.

canal_p10_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_031.text: The low water exposed the dark edge while the crew stayed outside the pocket. Bao pointed out fine old cord fibers caught near the ruler's foot. They carried moisture above the visible surface by wicking, making the line look like a rise beyond its measured height. The ruler also leaned slightly after its clay seating softened. Neither defect had shifted the fitted stop. Both made the original reading less dependable than the dry inspection suggested. Yue copied the two observations separately instead of choosing the easier single cause.

canal_p10_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_032.text: Luo used the geared manual release to close the side outlet after the pocket emptied. The loaded powered path was isolated before anyone touched the measuring mount. Bao reset the ruler against the independent fixed masonry reference and removed the reachable old fibers with a long tool from stable paving. The clay edge would remain outside the accepted measuring face. The observer said he was sorry again. Yue told him the wetting had revealed a real measurement problem, and his call had given them time to find it within their limits.

canal_p10_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_033.text: The live interval ended before the observer's booked boat. He signed his offered account and received the accepted work acknowledgment, then walked to the landing without being asked to stay for Yue's recovered command. A follow-up on the twenty-third morning would fit Jiang's remaining actual trial hours. Today's powered drain and tomorrow's repeated response would remain inside the eighteen-unit supply maximum. Yue needed her own recovery before another live command. The delay cost a booked interval, but nobody's personal route became its hidden price.

canal_p10_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_034.text: A spectator called the first trial a failure as the crew covered the prepared pocket. Tian said it had found a fault before that fault directed a larger test. Yue still felt the word sting. She had made the commanded release cleanly, yet the successful motion had ended a question sooner than she wanted. Jiang asked for the actual gauge count and wrote eight used, two hundred eight remaining. The number was neither praise nor blame. It recorded what the machine had actually spent before everyone went to lunch.

canal_p10_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_035.text: Yue spent the afternoon on ordinary copying while her opened routes settled. She kept the observer's apology in his offered account but not in the technical fault description. The cord fibers and leaning ruler belonged there; his embarrassment did not cause the wet mark. At supper, he passed the counter on his returning boat and asked whether tomorrow's result would be sent to his receiver. Luo said yes. His work would have an ending he could learn without standing beside the bank until every question felt finished.

canal_p10_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_036.text: On the twenty-third morning, the fixed measuring face matched the independent masonry mark after a fresh low-water check. Bao inspected the stop and catch before Luo admitted the limited feed. Yue's ordinary baseline showed her route recovered. Jiang accepted one fresh prepared command at the full checked depth. The pocket filled to its twenty-centimetre mark without the misleading wick line. Its volume matched the bounded measurement within the test tolerance. Yue watched it reach the mark, then waited for the operator's actual call instead of celebrating early.

canal_p10_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_037.text: The second side-release response used ten counted supply units as the fuller pocket drained into its checked catch. Yue's small command ended at the scheduled release, with the actuator carrying the work. The lower stop stayed closed above the gardens, and the ordinary ground route remained clear. Bao checked the fitted witness marks after the water fell. Luo closed the side-release on its geared manual mechanism and repeated the ordinary seating check. The current bounded pocket had answered its test without sending a new question toward anyone's planted beds.

canal_p10_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_038.text: Jiang recorded eighteen trial supply units used across the two live responses, leaving one hundred ninety-eight from the original supply. The apparatus's actual gauge supported the count. Yue copied the first early stop and the successful follow-up as a sequence, preserving the altered measuring mount rather than hiding yesterday beneath today's cleaner result. The morning-only observer's receiver would get the approved follow-up. The report accepted only this bounded pocket and side-release under the checked head. The whole flood route remained a separate unfinished job.

canal_p10_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_039.text: Yue sent the follow-up through the appointed landing receiver before joining the common review. Her arms needed recovery after the fresh command, and she took ordinary notes slowly. Bao had the cord fragments wrapped beside the corrected ruler drawing. Tian brought the viewing-place report, including the spectator's mistaken claim that nothing useful happened. Yue did not want that claim erased from everybody's memory by a speech. She wanted the actual sequence available, where a person who cared could see what changed between two mornings.

canal_p10_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_040.text: Luo kept the feeder closed while Bao compared the held pocket's visible surface with the fixed masonry reference from stable paving. Jiang left the actuator isolated and Yue used an ordinary sighting rod. The water stayed below the accepted maximum. The side ruler had leaned a little as its clay seating softened, while fine old cord fibers at its foot wicked moisture upward. The dark line looked higher than the actual surface. The observer's call remained useful because neither dry inspection nor the original drawing had explained those changed wet conditions.

canal_p10_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_041.text: Bao would not repair the ruler beside held water merely because they now knew its fault. Luo opened the side-release with its geared ordinary manual mechanism and drained into the checked catch. Jiang kept the powered supply isolated. The lower stop above the gardens remained seated. Once the pocket emptied, Bao reset the ruler from the independent masonry reference and removed the reachable fibers from stable paving. Yue copied the actual new support and mark. They had used time and ordinary effort, with no apparatus charge drawn yet.

canal_p10_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_042.text: The morning-only observer still had part of his accepted interval left after the correction. Luo asked whether he wanted to watch the repeated bounded fill within that remaining time, making clear his paid ending would not move if it ran long. He agreed. Jiang confirmed the current mechanical checks after the dry correction. Yue's prepared command remained unused and her route recovered. The bank could try the checked full-depth response today, stopping again if another unexplained reading appeared. The observer looked less apologetic when asked rather than retained.

canal_p10_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_043.text: The refilled pocket reached the fixed twenty-centimetre mark without the misleading wick line. Its checked volume stayed within the accepted tolerance. Bao confirmed the lower stop and side-release path, and Jiang gave the prepared-response call. Yue made the quarter-unit command within her half-unit delivery allowance. The actuator opened the side outlet into the catch with a ten-unit draw. The actual water left under ordinary observation. Yue released at the scheduled point and let her routes settle while Luo used the geared manual mechanism for the dry closing check.

canal_p10_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_044.text: The fitted stop's witness marks remained steady, and the independent surface reference matched the corrected ruler. The observer gave his final reading without adding an apology. Jiang accepted the current bounded response and entered ten supply units used, leaving two hundred six. The early stop, dry correction and successful response all fit inside today's agreed cargo hold and worker intervals. Yue did not call the faster route superior to a longer investigation they might have needed. It was the path today's actual observations had permitted.

canal_p10_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_045.text: The observer left for his boat at the stated time with the offered report receiver written on his copy. His stopping call remained beside the actual fault description. At the public viewing place, Tian corrected a spectator who claimed the worker had wasted everyone's morning. The changed ruler and removed wick fibers would be described in the approved report. The observer did not need to stay and defend himself. Yue was grateful for that, because defending a useful call could easily become more exhausting than making it under pressure.

canal_p10_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_046.text: After lunch, Yue rested her opened routes and copied the apparatus gauge from Jiang's accepted count. The pocket remained isolated while Bao checked the repaired measuring mount again after drying. Its current fixed support held the mark. The upper trial had used less than its conservative eighteen-unit supply allowance, and the unspent difference stayed in the case. A budget could remain partly unused without proving somebody planned badly. Yue liked seeing a little resource left because a problem was examined before an unnecessary powered repetition.

canal_p10_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_047.text: On the twenty-third morning, Luo and Bao performed the ordinary follow-up at the emptied pocket. The ruler matched its masonry reference, the wick material was gone and the stop's marks remained seated. No live powered response was needed merely to fill another appointment. Jiang's accepted remaining reporting hours completed the trial handover and supply record. Yue's route baseline had recovered after yesterday's single command. She felt disappointed at the absence of another performance, then used her recovered hands to draw a clearer maintenance diagram for the next keeper.

canal_p10_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_048.text: Jiang retained the apparatus case with two hundred six actual units and accepted only the bounded pocket's current response. The lower garden route remained closed pending its agreed visit. Yue read the draft report aloud, separating the unexplained first wet mark from a genuine excessive head they had not observed. The observer's stop was correct under the rule even though the eventual cause was measurement behavior. Tian asked for that sentence in plain speech on the public version. Yue made it plain before the report left the counter.

canal_p10_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_049.text: Yue joined the common review with the approved supply count, corrected ruler drawing and actual worker ending preserved. She had made one small live command, then let the ordinary follow-up remain ordinary. Bao wrapped the cord fragments beside the report. Luo prepared the garden visit's current route notes. The trial had ended within its resources and actual time, leaving a useful acceptance and an unfinished wider question. Yue could accept both without trying to turn the day into a threshold her body or the channel had not crossed.

canal_p10_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_050.text: Yue said the bank should end today's live interval and examine the reading before asking its workers for another result. Luo confirmed the feeder closed and the lower stop above the gardens seated. She opened the side-release with the ordinary geared manual mechanism into the checked catch. Jiang kept the powered supply isolated. The pocket drained without spending apparatus charge or Yue's prepared command. The decision disappointed spectators who had waited for a glow. It kept the test inside the ordinary control that had already been accepted for this small head.

canal_p10_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_051.text: The morning-only observer gave his offered account before leaving for the booked boat. He said he feared the wet line showed a rise beyond the ruler, and wanted the later findings sent to his actual receiver. Yue thanked him for the call and kept its uncertainty visible. Tian heard a spectator call the ending cowardly and told him the test was not a competition. The observer walked away while the criticism still existed. The bank would have to answer it with a result, rather than hold him until the crowd approved.

canal_p10_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_052.text: Once the pocket emptied, Bao compared the ruler with the independent fixed masonry reference. Its clay seating had softened and allowed a slight lean. Fine cord fibers near the foot wicked moisture above the surface and made the dark line look like rising head. He reset the measuring support, removed the reachable fibers from stable paving and marked the corrected face. Yue copied both causes. Her unused command could not have told them these things more quickly than the ordinary rod and emptied pocket already had.

canal_p10_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_053.text: Jiang rebooked the short live follow-up within her actual remaining trial hours for the twenty-third morning. Today's ended interval would not create another paid worker-day by itself. The keeper arranged the small cargo hold and notified its ordinary receivers. The observer chose not to return because another booked job needed him, and his relay partner accepted the reading position under her own available hours. Yue saw a schedule change that respected one person's departure while giving another person a real task rather than a borrowed household name.

canal_p10_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_054.text: At lunch, Han complained about the second cargo hold. Luo showed its short booked interval and alternatives. He asked whether Yue had stopped because she doubted her own command. She said the unexplained reading needed examination before the powered response. Her route had been ready, but readiness did not settle the pocket's behavior. Han considered that and said he wished he had waited for the original heading before making his sale notice. Yue let the comparison stand without pretending the two decisions had identical stakes.

canal_p10_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_055.text: Yue spent the afternoon on the corrected handover drawing and kept personal practice brief. The prepared live command remained unspent; she did not owe the interrupted schedule a private demonstration in her room. Tian brought the public viewing report and asked whether she regretted ending the interval. Yue said she regretted the inconvenience and still supported the decision. The two feelings could coexist. Tian said she understood after the hearing. They folded the corrected report cover before supper, leaving tomorrow its actual chance rather than rehearsing a victory.

canal_p10_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_056.text: On the twenty-third morning, the replacement observer read the corrected ruler from its stable paving position. Luo checked the current feeder head and admitted the limited water. The pocket reached its twenty-centimetre mark without the misleading wick line, and its measured volume stayed within tolerance. Jiang checked Yue's ordinary recovered baseline and called for the one prepared response. The quarter-unit command ran within its half-unit delivery allowance. The side actuator opened into the checked catch, using ten supply units while the fixed lower stop protected the gardens.

canal_p10_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_057.text: Jiang used a further two counted units for the accepted powered dry-closing comparison after the pocket emptied, then isolated the supply. Luo repeated the ordinary manual-equivalent check with its geared handle. Both current control methods moved the small side-release as designed under their tested conditions. Yue released her route at the scheduled end and rested while Bao inspected the fixed witness marks. The trial used twelve actual units from the two hundred sixteen available at its start, leaving two hundred four in the original six stones.

canal_p10_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_058.text: The report retained today's successful follow-up beside yesterday's deliberately ended interval. It showed the ruler's changed support and removed wick fibers, as well as the actual supply count and replacement observer's accepted hours. The first observer's receiver would receive the approved result without a demand that he return to hear praise. Yue asked for the public report to say that the early ending followed an unexplained reading under the stopping rule. It would not be called a failed command, because no command had been attempted then.

canal_p10_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_059.text: Yue joined the common review with her route recovering and the case holding two hundred four actual units. The bank had accepted this bounded pocket and side-release, while the larger garden route remained closed. Bao placed the old cord fragments beside the corrected ruler drawing. Tian carried the approved public viewing note. Yue knew the extra day had cost two short cargo holds and different worker availability. She would preserve those consequences even though the final response now looked like the result everybody wanted at first light.

canal_p10_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_060.text: The common trial review assembled the actual sequence chosen by the crew, with its precise supply count in Jiang's signed gauge record. Every permitted path preserved the observer's stopping call and found the ruler's wet seating and old wick fibers. The repaired measurement now matched the fixed masonry reference. The conservative lower supply bound stood at one hundred ninety-eight, while the actual remaining count stayed separately recorded. The pocket's acceptance covered its small checked head and catch route. Nothing in that report opened the channel toward the gardens.

canal_p10_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_061.text: Luo posted the plain public findings before cargo resumed its ordinary pattern. The trial had found and corrected a measurement fault, then accepted the bounded side-release response. The garden closure remained. Spectators could ask for the fuller current report at the counter rather than build their conclusions from a remembered early stop. Tian read the plain version once and nodded. Yue had wanted a story in which she did everything right. The posted account showed a crew using an interruption well enough to discover what it had not known.

canal_p10_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_062.text: Han checked his private loading times against the actual trial holds and recorded one rearranged customer turn. He did not create a fee against the common receiver merely because the stop inconvenienced his business. The later gear lease still needed its complete ordinary observation week. Its proposed monthly four copper would pay specified useful services, with remedies for nonperformance. Yue asked whether he found all the bounded agreements exhausting. He said yes, but they were beginning to be less expensive than a single grand offer he could not lawfully deliver.

canal_p10_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_063.text: The morning-only observer's landing receiver collected the approved follow-up and confirmed its ordinary delivery route. His stopped interval, accepted work and chosen departure remained in the record. The receiving note did not promise every future test would need him. Yue felt glad that the useful call could reach its own ending. A person had seen something unexplained, spoken under the procedure and gone to another paid boat. The bank could remember that without turning him into either an embarrassed obstacle or a permanent guardian of its water.

canal_p10_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_064.text: Bao checked the ruler support once more as the pocket dried. He fitted the current removable mount so later measurements would reference stable masonry instead of soft clay. The old cord fibers went to the retained fault packet; reachable debris stayed cleared. Ordinary future checking still had a receiver. Yue drew the new mount with its fixing faces visible and left the decorative shadow out of the service diagram. Beauty belonged in her private margin. The next keeper needed to know where a small ruler could begin lying again.

canal_p10_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_065.text: Pei asked Yue to explain the trial volume without invoking the valley's drinking-water crisis. The canal's twenty-four ten-litre equivalents described current ordinary test water, with its separate source and return route. It had no claim over household jars elsewhere. Yue had not made that confusion in her own notes, but one spectator had. The public clarification would keep the analogy from wandering farther. Pei said numbers traveled farther than their containers. Yue smiled and kept the actual container reference beside the measurement in the report.

canal_p10_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_066.text: A garden messenger reached the counter with news that one planting household wanted the survey postponed until its owner returned on the twenty-fifth day. The original twenty-fourth visit could still observe the public upper boundary with the current garden correspondent, but no inspection of that household's private drainage cut would occur in the owner's absence. Luo accepted the two-step visit. The trial acceptance did not entitle the bank to hurry private ground. Yue packed for an ordinary survey that would need more listening than a ruler could provide.

canal_p10_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_067.text: Jiang completed the accepted reporting hours and prepared to leave the apparatus case at its assigned commission store. Any later live frame use would require a new booked qualified appointment and actual unspent funds; her original three worker-day equivalents were now complete. The remaining case supply belonged to the commission, with the precise trial-path count preserved. Yue asked who could operate it during a future emergency. Jiang gave the ordinary workshop receiver and her available contact, which was a way to seek help rather than a promise that she would appear instantly.

canal_p10_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_068.text: Luo sent the apparatus receiver the current acceptance and asked for a separately priced standby response if higher-water warnings arrived later. The reply would need funding before a fresh appointment could be counted. The regular operations account could carry the ordinary message; it could not conceal a new crew's wages inside the already complete three-day allocation. Yue put the proposed standby request in the future-work section. The bank had learned enough from its bounded trial to ask a more concrete question, and that question still had an actual price.

canal_p10_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_069.text: At the gate, Bao and Luo reviewed the current ordinary fastening marks while waiting for the survey boat fare. The larger spill repair would need ground beyond their pocket, where an old seasonal diversion use met current private cultivation. The charter preserved a route, but landslides and new drainage altered where water would run. Yue found the old dark high-water mark less comforting each time she thought about it. Its survival meant something happened here once. It did not promise that the same flood would respect a drawing made before the ridge moved.

canal_p10_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_070.text: Tian brought a small travel roll sewn from the paid sail order's remaining approved offcut. Yue offered its ordinary stitching price, and Tian accepted. The roll held the survey pegs and kept their sharp ends away from Yue's patched pouch. Tian said she would stay to finish a new market order instead of joining the gardens visit. Yue was disappointed because she liked having her there. She asked for the order's actual delivery time rather than making friendship another invitation impossible to decline. Tian told her, and they planned supper afterward.

canal_p10_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_071.text: Han checked the reserved surplus goods before closing his store. The hoist and four planks stayed dry, with the cooper's removable tags still readable. His thirty-two private copper remained available toward the forty-eight deposit return; the promised sixteen delivery payment had not arrived. The twenty-four public installment remained reduced in the current fifty-six debt account. Yue did not need to recopy those sums tonight. She knew where the actual records stood, and could spend the evening thinking about people who would meet her below the fork.

canal_p10_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_072.text: The down-fork correspondent's map showed planted beans where the old spill sketch left open pale ground. Yue imagined a household seeing water directed toward rows it had tended for months and understood why a distant charter would not feel like an answer. Bao would inspect present levels, and Luo would bring the protected seasonal-use wording. Neither could make a person welcome a loss by showing that the canal had a right to ask about a route. A working arrangement would need changed choices and consequences on both banks.

canal_p10_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_073.text: The survey boat was an ordinary scheduled passage with room for the current team and light instruments. Its official fare belonged to the canal operating account, recorded within the review-term budget. Yue would travel with Bao for the current field comparison, while Luo joined through her keeper replacement arrangement. The replacement was an ordinary named operator already paid in the keeper schedule. The gate would remain under actual supervision instead of resting on an empty chair because its most familiar keeper went to speak about a different reach.

canal_p10_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_074.text: Before supper, Pei read the scratch-through name request aloud to its new possible receiver, who had heard of the trial and came to ask about records. He held no matching counterfoil but thought an older resident across the fork might know the household. The offered lead would travel through an ordinary request, not a compulsory search of cupboards. Yue wrote the contact beside her route without promising to answer it before the survey. The old pledge stayed released. The missing name could wait for its own truthful path.

canal_p10_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_075.text: At supper, Bao admitted he had expected the ruler to be the easy part of the trial. Luo said she expected the feeder's gritty pin, which the ordinary dry check had already caught. Yue admitted she expected her own command to be the central question. Each had guessed differently before the water entered. They laughed at the crooked collection of predictions. The report was better because it recorded observations afterward rather than arranging itself around whichever person felt most confident before breakfast.

canal_p10_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_076.text: Yue made her ordinary recovery check before sleep and accepted the result without repeating it for reassurance. Her earned second pair remained what it had been on arrival. She had used a small route within its allowance and seen how much of a useful test belonged to other people, fixed wood and a gauge mounted badly. The apparatus did not make her smaller. It gave her a more accurate place in the work. Tomorrow that place would be beside people who had not watched the trial and owed her no applause for it.

canal_p10_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_077.text: After the others left, Luo stayed at the counter mending the handle of her household cup with a strip of cord. Yue offered to find another cup in the store. Luo said she liked this one because its crooked handle fitted the old bend of her finger. The repair would hold ordinary tea, and she would stop using it if the crack widened. Yue sat beside her without making an argument about replacement costs. They listened to the last departing boat while the keeper tied a familiar small thing back together.

canal_p10_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p10_078.text: The counter lamp stayed lit while the final approved copies dried. The upper pocket was empty, its current side-release closed and the lower garden stop still seated. Cargo used the ordinary repaired gate again. Han's store remained private, Tian's room remained hers and Pei's amended ledger carried both completion and the still-open missing name. Yue packed the survey roll in her habitual bag. On the twenty-fourth morning, she would go below the fork and learn what their water looked like from ground it had not yet been allowed to cross.
